newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

More consumption of rice flour-based food items will save the country billions in foreign exchange, and help paddy farmers to get a good price for their crop, said K.B.Palipana, general manger, Paddy Marketing Board. A wheat flour subsidy now in force, costs the government millions a year.
Army Commander Lieutant General Daluwatte says recent drive to recruit soldiers, meets with massive response mainly from rural youth.
Nation bids farewell to former president J.R.Jayewardene, who died on Friday at the age of 90.

Police arrest a Sri Lankan born Canadian, who was allegedly planning to dupe students from Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Bangladesh, India and Malaysia, with a bogus two-year diploma in information technology from a non-existent institute in Canada, police sources say.
Former President J.R.Jayeardene, who died on Friday, to be cremated on banks of Kelani river today.
Police Special Task Force finds LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam) arms cache in north central Monaragala jungles.
Government to speed up building of Colombo-Katunayake expressway.
